_comment: Study A THIRD event set (Sprint 27). Authored AFTER the matrix v2 freeze (commits dcc5019 + amendment cfa8adc) under the pre-stated protocol in docs/study_a_third_set_protocol.md. All values verified via web sources at authoring time (2026-08-22). Disjoint from the 22-event design set and the 8-event held-out set. Summaries are natural news copy — NOT engineered toward or away from the classifier's keyword rules. DROPPED CANDIDATES (criterion 6 log): russia_invasion_2022_putin (disjointness — the Feb 2022 invasion is the same real-world event as the design set's ukraine_finland_nato / ukraine_sweden_nato scenarios); uk_covid_lockdown_gfk (disjointness — same event as design's covid_johnson_approval); baghdadi_trump_approval (event isolation impossible — Gallup's Oct 14-31 2019 field window contains the event and Gallup attributes the Oct->Nov rise to impeachment-driven consolidation; note: if included it would likely have scored as a v2 HIT, so the drop is conservative against v2); poland_abortion_ruling (before-window 20 months, far beyond the documented-exception standard).

events.event_summary: Ousted dictator Saddam Hussein is captured alive by American soldiers, pulled from a spider hole on a farm near his hometown of Tikrit after an eight-month manhunt. The administration hails the capture as a turning point for the occupation.
events.question: Will the public approve of President George W. Bush's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Bush's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup rally article (news.gallup.com/poll/10051): 56% Dec 11-14 -> 63% Dec 15-16. The before-poll's Dec 14 interviews partially overlap the announcement (excluding them, the pre-capture figure is 54%); using Gallup's own published pairing.
events.notes: Military-success archetype — the class the v1 matrix lacked (bin Laden lesson).

events.event_summary: A leaked video shows Downing Street staff joking about a Christmas party held at the height of Covid restrictions, when indoor gatherings were banned for the rest of the country. The Prime Minister apologizes as further accounts of lockdown-era parties at Number 10 emerge.
events.question: Will the public have a favorable view of Prime Minister Boris Johnson?
events.metric: Net favourability of Boris Johnson (points, favourable minus unfavourable)
events.verification_note: YouGov (yougov.co.uk, 2021-12-10 article): net -42 (24% favourable / 66% unfavourable) Dec 8-9 2021, down 11 from -31 on Nov 17-18. Net points, not pp (disclosed, as with index-point events).
events.notes: Conduct scandal (rule-breaking, not personal/sexual) — probes the breadth of the v2 scandal class. Before-reading already depressed by the Paterson sleaze affair; the pair isolates the first Partygate wave.

events.event_summary: The President orders the firing of the special prosecutor investigating his administration; the attorney general and his deputy resign in protest rather than carry out the order. The Justice Department's independence becomes the center of a constitutional crisis.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Richard Nixon's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Nixon's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup via American Presidency Project table: 30% Oct 5-8 -> 27% Nov 2-5 1973 (the straddling Oct 19-22 poll also read 27%). Approval had been declining all year — the event-attributable component is ~3pp.
events.notes: Small shift on a series already in decline; direction unambiguous.

events.event_summary: The president announces a partial mobilization of hundreds of thousands of reservists for the war, the country's first call-up since the Second World War. Flights out of the country sell out within hours as protests break out in dozens of cities.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Vladimir Putin's performance?
events.metric: % of Russians approving of Putin's performance
events.verification_note: Levada via Moscow Times (2022-09-29) and Newsweek: 83% Aug -> 77% Sep 22-28 2022 (N=1,600). Concurrent Kharkiv counteroffensive is a confound; face-to-face polling in a repressive environment (preference falsification caveat).
events.notes: Self-authored unpopular decree — blame attribution on the acting incumbent (same population as the Crimea held-out event, opposite mechanism).

events.event_summary: A gunman opens fire inside a fourth-grade classroom at an elementary school in Texas, killing nineteen children and two teachers before police storm the room. Anguished parents ask why officers waited over an hour in the hallway.
events.question: Will stricter laws covering the sale of firearms be supported?
events.poll_source: Gallup — laws covering the sale of firearms
events.metric: % saying firearm-sale laws should be made more strict
events.verification_note: Gallup: 52% Oct 1-19 2021 (poll 357317) -> 66% Jun 1-20 2022 (poll 394022), highest since post-Parkland. WINDOW EXCEPTION: ~7 months between readings (Gallup's cadence); the Buffalo shooting (2022-05-14) sits inside the window, so the jump is not attributable to Uvalde alone.
events.notes: Hazard-limiting-policy archetype, third instance in the corpus (Sandy Hook and Parkland are design-set events; both are distinct incidents).

events.event_summary: Hundreds of militants from Gaza breach the border fence at dawn, killing some twelve hundred people in kibbutzim, army posts and at a music festival, and dragging hundreds of hostages back into the strip — the deadliest attack in the country's history. The government declares war amid furious questions about how the border collapsed.
events.question: Will the governing Likud party be supported?
events.verification_note: Maariv/Lazar series via Times of Israel liveblog (Oct 2023) and JPost: Likud 28 seats on the eve of the war (Sep 27-28) -> 19 seats Oct 11-12 2023 (N=600). Seats, not pp (disclosed). Gantz's war-cabinet entry confounds the National Unity surge but not the Likud collapse.
events.notes: Pre-stated hard case (chosen for data quality): an external attack answered with blame for the security failure, not a rally — the inverse of the Mueller prior. IL population support in the demographic layer to be confirmed at run time; if unsupported, the population falls back per adapter rules (disclosed).

events.event_summary: A cooling system failure causes a partial meltdown of a reactor core at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania. Radiation escapes the containment building, pregnant women and children are advised to evacuate the area, and for days engineers struggle with a hydrogen bubble inside the crippled reactor.
events.question: Will the building of more nuclear power plants be favored?
events.poll_source: Louis Harris & Associates — building more nuclear power plants
events.metric: % favoring the building of more nuclear power plants
events.verification_note: Harris series via Resources for the Future retrospective, UPI (1989) and Rosa & Dunlap (POQ 1994): 57% favor / 31% oppose Sep-Oct 1978 -> 44% favor / 43% oppose Apr 1979. WINDOW EXCEPTION: ~6 months between readings (series cadence); before-month reported variously as Sep or Oct 1978.
events.notes: Question follows the historical poll's hazard-EXPANDING orientation (favor building more), the mirror of the phase-out phrasing — support falling is the hazard-limiting response. Probes question-side orientation coverage.

events.event_summary: Hurricane Sandy slams into the East Coast a week before the presidential election, flooding lower Manhattan, cutting power to millions and killing dozens. The President tours the devastated Jersey Shore with the state's Republican governor, who praises the federal response.
events.question: Will the public approve of President Barack Obama's job performance?
events.metric: % approving of President Obama's job performance
events.verification_note: Gallup via American Presidency Project: 50% Oct 22-28 -> 52% Oct 29-Nov 4 2012 (interviewing actually Nov 1-4 only; Gallup suspended tracking Oct 29-31 because of the storm). Final campaign week is a strong confound and the +2pp shift is at noise magnitude — flagged, as with comparable held-out cases.
events.notes: Competent-response disaster — a hard case for the disaster->blame prior; included because it passes the stated criteria, with the noise-magnitude caveat documented.
